thread:
maria: Quick dump from this morning's profiling run — FlashAttention variants, fused kernels, and paged-attn across our long-context workload. TL;DR: FlashAttention2 (FA2) is the fastest for 512–2048 tokens on A100s with fp16, fused kernels win on a few medium configs, and paged attention is the only viable path >8k but has high kernel launch overhead for small batches. Full notes + artifacts below.

ajay: Can you drop the raw numbers and where you ran them?

maria: Ran on a 4xA100-40G (DGX-ish) non-preemptible cluster, CUDA 11.8, drivers matching prod. Batches: 1, 4, 16. Seq lenses: 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 16384. Models: 7B-ish transformer (32 heads, head_dim=64). Dtype: fp16 unless noted.

maria: Benchmark excerpt (latency p50, ms) — small table:
```
# kernel | b=1 seq128 | b=1 seq512 | b=1 seq2048 | b=1 seq8192
FA2        6.2ms         9.8ms          24.5ms         142ms
FusedAttn  6.4ms        10.1ms          29.0ms         210ms
PagedAttn  9.1ms        15.3ms          60.2ms         98ms
```
Notes: FA2 shows ~1.8x over fused at 2048. PagedAttn becomes competitive at 8k+ for memory but has ~2x kernel overhead for short seqs.

maria: Now KV cache layout microbench (what I changed locally): tested two layouts — interleaved (per token: [head0_k..headN_k][head0_v..headN_v]) vs separate (all K arrays contiguous per head then V). Results for generation (autoregressive, batch=1, expanding seq):
```
layout    | p50 gen step (ms) (seq growing to 2k)
interleaved | 3.6ms
separate     | 4.9ms
```
Interpretation: interleaved gave ~35% lower per-step time for single-GPU generation because GPU loads were more coalesced across heads during KV read.

ajay: Interesting. Did you change alignment/stride? Also dtype?

maria: Yes — interleaved used 256-byte aligned allocations and 128-byte head stride (padded). Separate was compact per-head (no padding). I also tried bf16 (same throughput ±2% vs fp16) but fp16 had slightly lower p99 due to better kernel specialization.

shannon: Padding to 256 bytes sounds large. Why 256? Does it actually reduce bank conflicts?

maria: Two reasons: 1) cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels and our memcpy paths like aligned >128 often vectorize better. 2) For some kernels we saw unaligned LDG/STS generating extra instructions on Ampere; 256 avoids that corner. I can paste the microbench that toggles alignment:
```
for align in [64,128,256]:
  alloc(alignment=align)
  run_kv_read_benchmark()
  print(align, p50)
# results: 64->4.1ms, 128->3.8ms, 256->3.6ms
```

carl: Heads-up — my last rollout toggled a fused-attn heuristic (force-fused for seq<256) and we saw a ~7% p50 latency regression on chat workloads (batches often 2–4, seq 32–128). I think our selector picks fused too aggressively for small sequences / small batch.

maria: I saw that too — fused sometimes has better throughput but higher constant overhead for kernel launch / shared-mem setup on small inputs. Proposed selector rule: prefer FA2 for seq>=64 or when batch * seq >= 5120 tokens; otherwise prefer fused for medium bins where its vectorization helps. Also add a fast-path microbenchmark at startup to quickly pick best kernel per device.

ajay: Sounds good. For KV layout: interleaved looks better for single-GPU generation. How about multi-GPU sharded KV (model parallel)? Separate layout may map easier to shard. Any numbers?

maria: Right — separate layout gave easier sharding semantics and slightly lower cross-GPU copy overhead in our simulated sharded loop (+~0.7ms per step on NCCL allgather), whereas interleaved required a re-chunk + transpose before send. So: interleaved for single-GPU, separate for sharded multi-GPU, and add a lightweight convert path (async cuMemcpy + kernel transpose) when crossing boundary.

shannon: For commits: can we standardize an API flag: kv_layout: "interleaved|separate|auto" and kv_alignment_bytes: 64|128|256, default auto->256 on Ampere+?

maria: Agree. Also we should expose kv_dtype preference (fp16/bf16) and let kernel selector factor it in.

perf-bot: Uploaded full artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/perf/1768209456 — includes nvprof traces, kernel timelines, and the microbench harness. Note: two traces flagged as flaky (OOM) — ignore.

carl: Action items from my side: revert the fused-attn heuristic change and add the microbenchmark gating in the rollout pipeline.

maria: I'll add the kv-layout tests and conversion kernel + docs. I'll also push a small change to the selector to prefer FA2 for seq>=64 and add a startup perf probe.

ajay: Can someone add a short perf test for batch=1, seq growth patterns (simulate next-token gen) into the CI perf suite? That would catch regressions where layout/selector choices regress generation latency.

shannon: I'll add a perf job (nightly) and include alignment permutations. Keep notes in the perf ticket: #INF-1247.

maria: Thanks — will follow up with a short PR and link to the artifacts in the ticket. :thumbsup:
